item.title: Florida mandates sociology textbook that avoids race, gender — faculty call it censorship
item.description: Florida International University faculty are pushing back against the state over a newly mandated introductory sociology textbook, shortened to remove or reduce coverage of topics such as race, gender, and sexuality. An education expert told The College Fix the revisions do not necessarily amount to a fundamental alteration of the course. However, in a letter […]

item.title: What can you actually say? Understanding the boundaries of free expression on campus
item.description: The College Fix's Hannah Brady talks to the Foundation for Individual Rights and Education's Marie McMullen about the state of campus free speech, the biggest threats to free speech, how those threats have changed over time, and what the limits -- if any -- to free speech should be.

item.title: DEI remains strong at UMich a year after president promised to gut it
item.description: University of Michigan promised to get rid of DEI. It's still alive and kicking.

item.description: Lewis University protests could disrupt its operations.

item.title: Kansas could be next state to end in-state tuition for illegal immigrants
item.description: Kansas lawmakers are considering a bill to end in-state tuition for illegal immigrants, following Attorney General Kobach's warning of a potential lawsuit.

item.title: Stanford newspaper sues State Dept over international students’ right to free speech
item.description: A federal court is allowing a lawsuit by the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression to move forward against the Trump administration. The case argues that noncitizens in the U.S. legally should not fear deportation for their speech.

item.title: Foreign countries gave $67 billion to U.S. universities: Education Dept report
item.description: Qatar is the largest foreign donor to American universities, contributing $7.7 billion since 1986, according to a new U.S. Education Department report.

item.title: Police refute claim that black Virginia Tech professor was victim of racist attack
item.description: Police have refuted claims that a Virginia Tech professor was the victim of a racist attack, stating their investigation found no evidence of racial bias. The incident, involving juveniles throwing snow/ice and playing music, was deemed not targeted or threatening despite the professor's concerns over white youth singing along to racial slurs.
